scenario:
[LGRA.9.3.2]: `a < b < c` is `(a < b) and (b < c)`, and comparison operators may be mixed in one chain. One P fact holds a = 1, b = 2, c = 3, t = true and f = false.
- `ascending`, `p.a < p.b < p.c`, fires.
- `mixed`, `p.a < p.c > p.b`, is `(1 < 3) and (3 > 2)` and fires.
- `second_step_false`, `p.a < p.b > p.c`, is `(1 < 2) and (2 > 3)`, false, and must not fire.
- `bool_equalities` is the case that separates a chain from left-associative grouping. `p.f == p.f == p.t` as a chain is `(f == f) and (f == t)`, false. Grouped, it is `(f == f) == t`, which is `true == true`, true. So it must not fire.
- `bool_equalities_true`, `p.t == p.t == p.t`, is the control, true either way.
`dead_rules_expected` names the two that must not fire. Agenda order is source order ([LDET.5.4]). Path: the compiler expands the chain into its steps (`dsc.parse`'s chain production, [LGRA.9.3.1]). Both runtimes evaluate the expanded conjunction (libds rete/eval.c, Mercury ds.eval).
rules_ds:
schema P scope logical:
    id: String key
    a: Int mutable
    b: Int mutable
    c: Int mutable
    t: Bool mutable
    f: Bool mutable

rule ascending:
    P p where p.a < p.b < p.c
->
    log info "ascending"

rule mixed:
    P p where p.a < p.c > p.b
->
    log info "mixed"

rule second_step_false:
    P p where p.a < p.b > p.c
->
    log info "second_step_false"

rule bool_equalities:
    P p where p.f == p.f == p.t
->
    log info "bool_equalities"

rule bool_equalities_true:
    P p where p.t == p.t == p.t
->
    log info "bool_equalities_true"
